decisions.reason: The rejection reverses the actual local convention: def-qc-tqc-r-symbol defines R(f)=f composed with c^{-1}. Thus inverse precomposition in F2 and step 2.1 has matrix R, not R^{-1}; locality leaves all other vertex morphisms unchanged. Orthonormal grouped-tree decomposition and unitary reassociation give the asserted spectator action and norm bound.

The input already supplied endpoint isometries and an independent transport inequality, so the rejection overstates the gap. Its phrase physical action nevertheless mislabels the categorical target and left frame coordinates implicit. Replaced it with categorical action on V_cat and explicit Q_j, rho_log=Q_1^*rho(b)Q_0, iota_j=A_jQ_j^*. This preserves the independent transport premise and makes no realization inference from JRS.

Arbitrary isometries form an uncountable family even in a fixed nontrivial finite dimension, whereas finite strings are countable; the previous carrier supplied no exact finite encoding. Repaired the finite record to name a background isometry through a declared codebook; varying classical-input isometries require an explicit exact finite description language and fully charged description. Arbitrary abstract isometries remain available as fixed background model data, without a false universal finite-coordinate encoding.

The carrier delegated circuit and nonoracle costs to existing QC definitions but omitted them from its displayed record; N_prep alone counts no computational gates. Appended the complete applicable QC circuit cost record and a separate total nonoracle gate count, including description, wire, depth, ancilla, oracle and classical-family coordinates. Declared branch costs, overlaps and not-applicable conventions prevent zero-cost or double-counting interpretations.

The isolating-polynomial/interval data are a declared sufficient input representation for the finite implementation, not a claim of necessity for every SK algorithm or a conclusion drawn from Dawson–Nielsen. The actually used local published thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity states exactly these input hypotheses and supplies a proof using algebraic-coordinate bisection. Dawson–Nielsen section 3 indeed omits finite arithmetic; its caveat does not contradict this separately proved conditional interface. Determinants z^2 r=1, algebraicity, inverse closure, generated-subgroup density and supplied-net conventions all match the direct suppliers.

For the displayed positive-real superposition the probabilities and conditional vectors are correct. The zero-coefficient variation allows a surviving coefficient alpha of modulus one; its normalized conditional vector is alpha|a>, not literally |a>. Repaired step 2.1 to preserve that scalar and distinguish the vector from its pure-state ray. The zero-probability outcome still has no normalized conditional state.

The identity conclusion is correct, but F1 is existential for positive tolerance and does not itself give a zero-error guarantee for the particular empty word. Replaced that citation-dependent inference by the direct calculation: ambient identity fixes every code vector and has zero projection to its orthogonal complement. Determinant corrections are identities and exponent sum zero gives physical scalar one.

F1 literally called a finite alphabet dense, which is false; its supplier correctly proves density of the generated subgroup. Repaired F1 to state generated-subgroup density. The proof now uses exactly the standard inverse-closed dense gate-package hypothesis. Independently checked q_j=4096 eta_j, q_next=q_j^(3/2), existence of least J including J=0, logarithmic length exponent, the separate polynomial Cauchy-name/algebraic-input bit bound, and the retained physical scalar. Statement unchanged.

The old proof assumed all arbitrary U(2) and CNOT QSD factors already had delta approximations, without obtaining them from its stated facts; SK on SU(2) and exact QSD alone do not supply this. Added F5 from the already declared arbitrary-n approximation theorem, carrying its AComega and nonzero-spectator hypotheses. At tolerance delta/2 each factor has code-isometry error at most delta by adding its logical and leakage components. An explicit telescoping identity on code inputs now bounds the product by M delta <= epsilon/2 relative to the recorded product scalar. The numerical recurrence remains eta1=2^(-27/2), eta2=2^(-57/4), J=2 and length <=25 L0, with no B6 length bound.
